areas.h2: Okara neighbourhoods we know street by street
areas.lede: Every photograph below is a real place in Okara District — its chowks, parks, bazaars and landmarks. This is the city you'd actually be buying into.

cards.alt: Grounds of the Combined Military Hospital in Okara Cantonment
cards.p: The quietest, greenest address in the city. Wide streets, mature trees, cantonment upkeep. Buyers here look for 10 marla and 1 kanal.
cards.rate: Premium end of the Okara market

cards.alt: Company Bagh Chowk in central Okara at dusk
cards.p: Old Okara at its most central. Walk to the courts, schools and the main bazaar. Older houses, generous plot sizes, strong rental demand.
cards.rate: Best for: rental income, city-centre living

cards.alt: Jinnah Park Chowk, Okara, on a clear winter morning
cards.p: Families pay for the park and the schools around it. Depalpur Road behind it has been the city's steadiest growth direction.

cards.alt: Entrance gate of Mian Muhammad Zaman Public Park, Okara
cards.p: Planned society off the Lahore–Okara Road with small entry-level plots through to 1 kanal. Popular with first-time buyers and instalment plans.

cards.alt: Flour mills on the GT Road at Okara
cards.p: Okara's trading spine. Shops, showrooms, marriage halls, mills and godowns. Frontage in feet is what sets the price here, not covered area.

cards.alt: Ghausia Masjid in Katchery Bazar, Okara
cards.p: Dense, busy, and the highest per-marla commercial rates in the district. Small shops here trade on footfall alone.
cards.rate: Best for: retail shops, upper-floor offices

cards.alt: District Library building in Okara
cards.p: Older government housing and the surrounding colonies. Sensible prices, walkable to offices, and a reliable tenant pool.
cards.rate: Best for: budget houses, first purchase

cards.alt: Okara cricket stadium pavilion building
cards.p: Newer development along the canal side. Canal View and Canal Garden attract buyers who want a plot rather than an old house.
cards.rate: Best for: 3–10 marla plots, new build

cards.alt: Jamia Masjid Ghausia in Aziz Housing Scheme, Okara
cards.p: Aziz Housing Scheme, Gulberg City, Al Kheer City, Al Rehman Town, Saad City, Haider Town and Mehboob Town — we deal in all of them.
cards.rate: Best for: instalment plots, new construction

cards.alt: Passengers outside the brick arches of Okara Railway Station
cards.p: Colonial-era brickwork, tight lanes and constant movement. Mixed-use property that suits shops below and rented portions above.

cards.alt: A street in Depalpur city, Okara District
cards.p: One of the oldest towns in Punjab, and still the district's second market. Depalpur, Basirpur, Haveli Lakha and Hujra Shah Muqeem.
cards.rate: Best for: town houses, farmland, shops

cards.alt: Kalma Chowk in Renala Khurd, Okara District
cards.p: On the Okara–Lahore side of the district, with the fruit farms and the old hydel works. Khalid Town and Green City are the schemes buyers ask for.
cards.rate: Best for: plots, farmland, roadside commercial

process.h2: From first call to registry, in five steps
process.lede: Punjab's land record is digitised now. That is good news — it just means the checks happen in a specific order. Here's the order we follow.

steps.p: Area, size, budget and timeline. A five-minute call on WhatsApp saves three wasted visits.
We show you three or four that genuinely fit, and tell you what's wrong with each one.
Fard malkiat from the Arazi Record Centre, mutation history, society NOC and dues clearance — before any money moves.
Token money against a written agreement on stamp paper, with the balance date and penalties spelled out.
Taxes paid, biometric verification done, sale deed registered, keys handed over. We're there for all of it.

list: CNIC of buyer and seller (and NICOP for overseas Pakistanis)

about.h2: An Okara office, run by people from Okara
about.lede: Muhammad Properties has been dealing in Okara property since 2010, from an office on the GT Road opposite Azhar Residencies.
paras: Okara is not Lahore, and it does not behave like Lahore. It is a district of about 3.5 million people across three tehsils — Okara, Depalpur and Renala Khurd — built on potato, maize and cotton, on the Sahiwal cattle and Nili-Ravi buffalo herds, and on the trade that moves along the N-5. Prices here are set by which street you are on, whose family is selling, and whether the fard is clean. No portal can tell you that.
That is the whole job. We give you the local read on a property, we check the record before you commit a rupee, and we stay with the file until the registry is done and the keys are in your hand.
list: One point of contact from first viewing to final transfer
Record verification through the Arazi Record Centre, every time
Written agreements on stamp paper — never a verbal deal
Commission agreed in advance, in writing, with no surprises

faq.lede: The questions we're asked on the phone most weeks.

items.q: How much does a 5 marla house cost in Okara?
a: As at August 2026, 5 marla houses in Okara typically ask between PKR 70 lakh and PKR 1 crore. Areas such as Saad City, Depalpur Road and Jawad Avenue sit in that band. Smaller 2–3 marla houses in Faisal Colony or Government Colony start around PKR 25 lakh. The final figure turns on street width, construction quality and whether gas is connected.

items.q: Which areas of Okara are best for investment?
a: For capital growth, buyers focus on the newer schemes along Canal Road and the Lahore–Okara Road side — Canal View, Model Town Okara and Gulberg City — where plots are still available at development-stage prices. For rental income, the older central areas around Company Bagh, Civil Lines and the Railway Road hold tenants best. Okara Cantt Civil Area is the premium end and holds value, but entry is expensive.

items.q: What is a marla, and how does it compare to a kanal or an acre?
a: In Punjab, 1 marla is 225 square feet (25 square yards). 20 marla make 1 kanal, which is 4,500 square feet. 8 kanal make 1 acre. So a 5 marla plot is 1,125 square feet and a 10 marla plot is 2,250 square feet.

items.q: What documents do I need to buy property in Okara?
a: You'll need your CNIC (or NICOP if you're an overseas Pakistani), and from the seller: the original title document — registry, allotment letter or transfer letter — the fard malkiat or record of rights, a no-objection certificate and dues clearance from the housing society or TMA, the approved building plan for constructed property, and recent clear utility bills.
We obtain the fard from the Arazi Record Centre and check the mutation history before any payment is made.

items.q: What taxes and fees are payable on a property transfer in Punjab?
a: Expect stamp duty, the registration fee, capital value tax, TMA or district fees, and FBR advance tax — section 236K on the buyer and section 236C on the seller, charged at different rates for filers and non-filers. Housing societies also charge their own transfer fee.
These rates change with each federal budget and provincial notification, so we confirm the exact amount for your property on the day rather than quoting a stale figure.

items.q: Do you deal in agricultural land near Okara?
a: Yes. Okara District is farming country — it is one of the largest potato-producing districts in Pakistan, and also grows maize, cotton and fodder. We deal in cultivable land along the chak roads and canal distributaries in all three tehsils: Okara, Depalpur and Renala Khurd. Land is priced per acre, and we verify the khasra numbers, the watercourse rights, the tube well and the access road before you commit.

items.q: Can overseas Pakistanis buy property in Okara through you?
a: Yes, and a good share of our work is exactly this. We send video walkthroughs and record checks over WhatsApp, deal with your nominated family member here, and can work with a registered power of attorney where you cannot travel. We insist on payment through banking channels and on you seeing the fard yourself before anything is signed.

items.q: How long does a property sale take in Okara?
a: Where the record is clean and both parties are ready, four to six weeks from bayana to registry is normal. Add time if the property is inherited and shares need settling, if a society NOC is slow, or if the seller is abroad and a power of attorney has to be attested. We tell you at the outset which of these applies to your file.

items.q: Do you charge a commission, and how much?
a: Yes — property dealing in Okara works on commission, and we agree it in writing before we start rather than raising it at the closing table. What we charge depends on whether it is a sale, a purchase or a rental, and on the value of the property. Ask us on the first call and you will get a straight number.

items.q: Which areas does Muhammad Properties cover?
a: All of Okara District. In the city that means Okara Cantt, Civil Lines, Company Bagh, Katchery Bazar, Government Colony, Faisal Colony, Model Town, Jawad Avenue, Canal View and Canal Road, Gulberg City, Al Kheer City, Al Rehman Town, Aziz Housing Scheme, Saad City, Haider Town, Mehboob Town and the GT Road belt. Outside the city we cover Depalpur, Basirpur, Haveli Lakha, Hujra Shah Muqeem, Renala Khurd and the surrounding chaks.

items.q: Do you handle rentals as well as sales?
a: Yes — family houses, upper portions, bachelor accommodation, offices and shops. We screen tenants, support police verification, and put the tenancy on stamp paper with the rent, increment and notice period written down. It costs a little more at the start and saves a great deal later.

items.q: Where is your office and when are you open?
a: We are on the GT Road in Okara, opposite Azhar Residencies, open Monday to Saturday from 9am to 7pm. Call or WhatsApp +92 305 6847007, or email info@muhammadproperties.online. If you're travelling in from out of town, message first and we'll have the shortlist ready when you arrive.
